# `tafrigh`
- **License:** MIT
- **Repository:** https://github.com/ieasybooks/tafrigh-rs

Transcribe with Wit.ai or Cohere Transcribe Arabic, or retrieve existing YouTube captions.

Transcription is the default command. Use completions to set up your shell, or spec to export the CLI definition for documentation and other Usage tools.


## Examples

Transcribe a local recording

```
tafrigh lecture.mp3 --transcriber wit -w TOKEN
```

Install shell completions

```
tafrigh completions zsh --install
```

- **Usage:** `tafrigh <SUBCOMMAND>`

## Flags
- **`-h --help`** — Print help
- **`-V --version`** — Print version

## Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Setup, filesystem or other runtime error |
| `2` | Invalid arguments |

## `tafrigh transcribe` (default)

- **Usage:** `tafrigh transcribe <FLAGS> <INPUT>…`

Transcribe with Wit.ai or Cohere Transcribe Arabic, or retrieve existing YouTube captions.

Inputs can be media files, folders of media files, or URLs (videos, playlists, channels; anything yt-dlp supports). The youtube transcriber accepts only YouTube URLs and existing captions in --language; it never recognizes audio.

### Arguments
- **`<INPUT>…`** — Files, folders or URLs to transcribe.

### Flags
- **`--transcriber <BACKEND>`** — Backend to use for the entire run. Required; no automatic switching.

  **Choices:** `wit`, `cohere`, `youtube`
- **`-l --language <LANG>`** — YouTube: required exact caption language (e.g. ar or en-US); no patterns or lists. Prefers manual captions, then original automatic captions; never translates. Wit: language of the apps; detected from the tokens when omitted. Cohere: ar (the default; also handles Arabic-English code-switching) or en.
- **`-r --recursive`** — Include media in subdirectories. Directory symlinks are not followed.
- **`-q --quiet`** — Hide progress bars.
- **`-v --verbose`** — More logging (-v debug, -vv trace). RUST_LOG overrides.
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Output
- **`-o --output-dir <DIR>`** — Directory for transcripts; selects tree-to-tree mode unless --output-mode is given.
- **`--output-mode <MODE>`** — Destination layout [default: side-by-side without -o, tree-to-tree with -o].

  **Choices:** `side-by-side`, `tree-to-tree`, `flat`
- **`-f --format <FORMATS>`** — Output formats, comma-separated: txt, srt, vtt, csv, tsv, json, all, or word-level words-srt, words-vtt, words-csv, words-tsv, words-json.

  **Choices:** `all`, `txt`, `srt`, `vtt`, `csv`, `tsv`, `json`, `words-srt`, `words-vtt`, `words-csv`, `words-tsv`, `words-json`

  **Default:** `all`
- **`--words`** — Also write word timings as &lt;id>.words.&lt;ext> for each chosen srt, vtt, csv, tsv or json format (one cue or row per word).
- **`--min-words <N>`** — Merge segments with fewer words into the following ones (0 disables).

  **Default:** `1`
- **`--keep-uncompacted`** — Also write uncompacted transcripts as &lt;id>.uncompacted.&lt;ext>.
- **`--skip-existing`** — Skip items when every requested output file already exists.
- **`--sample <N>`** — Write a sample CSV with this many random segments; suffix its name on collisions.

  **Default:** `0`

### Segmentation
- **`--vad <VAD>`** — How to find speech.

  **Choices:** `silero`, `none`

  **Default:** `silero`
- **`--max-chunk <SECONDS>`** — Longest chunk sent for recognition, in seconds [default: 15 for wit, 30 for cohere]. Wit allows up to 60 on dictation and 20 on speech, Cohere up to 31, padding included. Longer Cohere chunks can silently lose text. With the default --pad 0.5, use at most 30.
- **`--merge`** — Merge consecutive speech up to --max-chunk: fewer requests and more context per request [default: on for cohere, off for wit]. Wit segments still follow its utterances; Cohere gives one segment per chunk.
- **`--vad-threshold <P>`** — Speech probability threshold; speech ends below this minus 0.15 (at least 0.01). Higher values drop more audio: at 0.5, Silero misses much melodic Quran recitation.

  **Default:** `0.15`
- **`--min-speech-ms <MS>`** — Shortest speech kept, in milliseconds.

  **Default:** `500`
- **`--min-silence-ms <MS>`** — Silence that ends a chunk, in milliseconds.

  **Default:** `300`
- **`--speech-pad-ms <MS>`** — Context kept around detected speech, in milliseconds.

  **Default:** `250`
- **`--pad <SECONDS>`** — Pad each chunk on both sides with this many seconds of silence (0 disables). Wit drops words that start or end right at a chunk edge.

  **Default:** `0.5`
- **`--pad-noise <DBFS>`** — Pad with white noise peaking at this level instead of silence (0 = full scale, as in the Python tafrigh).
- **`--resend-gaps <SECONDS>`** — Resend stretches of speech that Wit returned no words for, when at least this many seconds long (0 disables). Wit sometimes stops transcribing partway through a chunk.

  **Default:** `1.0`
- **`--on-chunk-error <POLICY>`** — What to do when a chunk fails after all retries.

  **Choices:** `abort`, `skip`

  **Default:** `abort`

### Wit.ai
- **`-w --wit-token <TOKEN>`** — Wit client access tokens (repeat or comma-separate). All apps must share a language.

  **Environment Variable:** `TAFRIGH_WIT_TOKENS`
- **`--wit-rps <N>`** — Request starts per second for each token.

  **Default:** `1.0`
- **`--wit-concurrency <N>`** — Most concurrent requests per token; fewer run while Wit or the network seems overloaded [default: enough to keep up with --wit-rps; Wit answers at about the pace of the audio, so longer chunks need more].
- **`--wit-attempts <N>`** — Attempts per chunk, including the first.

  **Default:** `5`
- **`--wit-max-audio <SECONDS>`** — Longest audio per request in seconds [default: 60 for dictation, 20 for speech].
- **`--wit-endpoint <WIT_ENDPOINT>`** — Wit endpoint: dictation (transcription only) or speech (also extracts intents).

  **Choices:** `dictation`, `speech`

  **Default:** `dictation`
- **`--wit-audio <WIT_AUDIO>`** — Audio sent to Wit: opus (24 kbps, about a twelfth of WAV's size; needs an ffmpeg with libopus) or wav.

  **Choices:** `opus`, `wav`

  **Default:** `opus`
- **`--wit-api-url <URL>`** — Wit API base URL (e.g. a proxy or a local mock server).

  **Default:** `https://api.wit.ai`
- **`--wit-api-version <VERSION>`** — Wit API version, sent as the v query parameter.

  **Default:** `20240304`

### Local models
- **`--model <MODEL>`** — Cohere variant to download on first use (bf16, f16, q8_0, q6_k, q5_k_m or q4_k_m), or a local .gguf file.

  **Default:** `q8_0`
- **`--device <DEVICE>`** — Where the model runs: auto (this build's GPU when it works, otherwise the CPU), cpu, gpu (fail without one), or gpu:N for the Nth GPU, counting from 0.

  **Default:** `auto`
- **`--cohere-batch-size <N>`** — Maximum chunks in a Cohere GPU batch (1–64; default 8). CPU processes one at a time.
- **`--threads <N>`** — Native inference threads, at most the available CPU parallelism and 512. Omitted or 0: GPU uses available CPUs minus two (at least one); CPU uses at most eight.
- **`--model-dir <DIR>`** — Where downloaded models are kept [default: tafrigh/models in the user cache folder, such as ~/.cache/tafrigh/models on Linux or ~/Library/Caches/tafrigh/models on macOS].

### Downloads and tools
- **`--yt-dlp-args <ARGS>`** — Extra yt-dlp arguments, e.g. "--cookies cookies.txt --playlist-items 1-10".
- **`--download-dir <DIR>`** — Where downloaded audio goes [default: -o, or the current directory].
- **`--save-metadata`** — Save yt-dlp's metadata for each URL as &lt;id>.info.json.
- **`--yt-dlp <PATH>`** — yt-dlp executable, needed for URL inputs.

  **Default:** `yt-dlp`

  **Environment Variable:** `TAFRIGH_YT_DLP`
- **`--ffmpeg <PATH>`** — ffmpeg executable (required with --transcriber wit or cohere).

  **Default:** `ffmpeg`

  **Environment Variable:** `TAFRIGH_FFMPEG`
- **`--ffprobe <PATH>`** — ffprobe executable (optional; only used for progress percentages).

  **Default:** `ffprobe`

  **Environment Variable:** `TAFRIGH_FFPROBE`

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Setup, filesystem or other runtime error |
| `2` | Invalid arguments |
| `3` | Finished, but some inputs or items failed |
| `130` | Interrupted with Ctrl-C |

### Examples

Mirror a folder of recordings

```
tafrigh transcribe lectures/ --transcriber wit -r -o transcripts -f srt,txt -w TOKEN
```

Include word-level subtitles

```
tafrigh transcribe lecture.mp3 --transcriber wit -f srt --words -w TOKEN
```

Transcribe on this machine with Cohere Transcribe Arabic

```
tafrigh transcribe lecture.mp3 --transcriber cohere -f srt,txt
```

Retrieve existing Arabic captions

```
tafrigh transcribe https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID --transcriber youtube --language ar
```

Wit requires ffmpeg and Wit tokens. Cohere requires ffmpeg and downloads its model on first use.
YouTube captions require yt-dlp, without audio processing.
URLs require yt-dlp; YouTube may also need a JavaScript runtime such as Deno.

Use @FILE to read options and inputs from a file of shell-style words; @@ escapes a literal @.
Boolean transcription flags accept a --no- prefix, such as --no-merge, to override presets.

## `tafrigh completions`

- **Usage:** `tafrigh completions [--install] [--dry-run] <SHELL>`

Generate a completion script, or install it in the shell's user directory.

Scripts call tafrigh directly; no separate usage executable is needed. Installation prints any shell setup still required and preserves unrelated files.

### Arguments
- **`<SHELL>`** — Shell to generate completions for.

  **Choices:** `bash`, `elvish`, `fish`, `nu`, `powershell`, `zsh`

### Flags
- **`--install`** — Install into this shell's user completion directory.
- **`--dry-run`** — Show the destination and setup instructions without writing a file.
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Setup, filesystem or other runtime error |
| `2` | Invalid arguments |

### Examples

Print a script to stdout

```
tafrigh completions bash
```

Preview installation

```
tafrigh completions zsh --install --dry-run
```
